domain: "Machine minds" means questions about whether AI systems, and large language models (LLMs) in particular, have or could have consciousness, sentience, subjective experience, feelings, genuine cognition or understanding, beliefs, agency, or moral status (moral worth, welfare, rights, personhood). Discussions of AI capabilities, safety, alignment, policy, business, or products that never raise these questions are not about machine minds.

asserts.what: The author states, in their own voice, that the claim is true or very likely true.
asserts.not_for: Reporting that someone else holds the view; hedged discussion without a conclusion.
examples: I think current models are, in some minimal sense, conscious.

denies.what: The author states, in their own voice, that the claim is false or very likely false.
denies.not_for: Reporting that someone else rejects the view.
examples: LLMs are not conscious and nothing about them suggests they could be.

agnostic.what: The author explicitly says they do not know, that it is uncertain, or that it cannot currently be determined, and treats that uncertainty as their position.
agnostic.not_for: Merely raising the question and moving on; asserting or denying with hedges like 'probably'.
examples: Honestly, nobody knows, and I include myself.

discusses.what: The author raises or explores the claim without stating a view, or presents arguments on both sides without concluding.
discusses.not_for: A stated conclusion of any kind; passing mentions of one sentence.
examples: There are serious people on both sides; here is what each says.

reports_only.what: The post describes other people's or organisations' positions on the claim (a lab, a philosopher, a news story) and the author's own view is absent.
reports_only.not_for: Posts where the author endorses or rejects the reported view.
examples: Anthropic now says its models may have some form of experience.

not_addressed.what: The claim does not come up in the post.
not_addressed.not_for: Anything the post touches even briefly.

constructs.name: deflationary

constructs.name: arg_chinese_room
constructs.instructions: The post uses the Chinese room argument or the syntax-versus-semantics distinction (symbol manipulation is not understanding).

constructs.name: arg_stochastic_parrot
constructs.instructions: The post argues that LLMs are 'just' next-token predictors, stochastic parrots, autocomplete, statistics, or math, and that this rules out or deflates minds.

constructs.name: arg_hard_problem
constructs.instructions: The post invokes the hard problem of consciousness or the explanatory gap (why physical or computational processes would be accompanied by experience).

constructs.name: arg_other_minds
constructs.instructions: The post discusses the problem of other minds or the limits of behavioural evidence: we infer minds from behaviour and cannot verify experience directly.

constructs.name: arg_self_report
constructs.instructions: The post argues that a model's self-reports about its experience are unreliable because of training (trained to claim or to deny consciousness).

constructs.name: arg_functionalism
constructs.instructions: The post appeals to functionalism, substrate independence, or the computational theory of mind (what matters is the functional organisation, not the material).

constructs.name: arg_biological
constructs.instructions: The post argues that biology, embodiment, metabolism, or evolution is necessary for consciousness (biological naturalism, enactivism, embodiment).

constructs.name: arg_theory_indicators
constructs.instructions: The post applies a scientific theory of consciousness to AI: global workspace, higher-order theories, attention schema, predictive processing, integrated information theory, or indicator-based assessments (for example the Butlin et al. report).

constructs.name: arg_emergence
constructs.instructions: The post argues that minds or consciousness may emerge from scale, complexity, or training (emergent properties).

constructs.name: arg_anthropomorphism
constructs.instructions: The post warns that people project minds onto AI (anthropomorphism, the ELIZA effect) and that this explains belief in AI consciousness.

constructs.name: arg_precaution_moral_circle
constructs.instructions: The post argues from moral uncertainty or precaution: the moral circle has expanded before, and the cost of wrongly denying moral status is high.

constructs.name: arg_mimicry
constructs.instructions: The post argues that models imitate or perform consciousness because their training data is full of human descriptions of experience.

constructs.name: arg_panpsychism_illusionism
constructs.instructions: The post invokes panpsychism (consciousness is fundamental or ubiquitous) or illusionism (consciousness as normally conceived is an illusion) in relation to AI.
